what_its_for: Trifarotene is a prescription cream used to treat acne (pimples and blemishes) on the face and body (trunk), including the back, chest, and shoulders. It belongs to a group of medicines called retinoids, which work by helping skin cells turn over more quickly and keeping pores from getting clogged.
how_to_take: Wash and gently dry your skin before applying. Use a thin layer of cream and spread it evenly over your entire face (forehead, cheeks, nose, and chin) and/or the affected areas on your body. Do NOT apply inside your mouth, eyes, nostrils, cuts, or broken skin. Wash your hands thoroughly after applying unless you are treating the hands. Apply once daily in the evening or at bedtime.
dosing: Apply a thin layer (about a pea-sized amount for the face, and up to 4 pea-sized amounts for the trunk/body) to the affected skin ONCE daily in the evening. Use only as much as needed to cover the area — more cream does not mean better or faster results.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, skip it and just apply your next dose the following evening at your regular time. Do NOT apply a double dose or extra cream to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze.
when_it_works: Most people begin to see improvement in their acne after about 4 weeks of regular use, but it may take up to 12 weeks (about 3 months) to see the full benefit. Be patient and keep using it every day as directed, even if you do not notice changes right away.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, mouth, nostrils, or on broken or irritated skin. Avoid waxing, threading, or using harsh hair-removal products on treated skin. Avoid using harsh, abrasive, or drying skin products (like strong toners, astringents, or scrubs) on the same area. Limit sun exposure and tanning beds — trifarotene can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Always use sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher) and wear protective clothing when going outside. Avoid applying to windburned or sunburned skin until it has healed.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you experience: severe redness, peeling, burning, or irritation that does not improve or gets worse; sunburn-like reaction; signs of an allergic reaction such as severe rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; skin becomes very dry or painful. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as retinoids can be harmful to an unborn baby.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use trifarotene if you are pregnant or trying to become pregnant. Retinoids can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Use effective birth control while using this medication and discuss this with your doctor. Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using if you are breastfeeding, as it is not known if trifarotene passes into breast milk. Children: The safety and effectiveness of trifarotene have been studied in patients 9 years of age and older for facial acne, and 12 years and older for trunk acne. It is not recommended for children younger than these ages. Elderly: No special precautions are known, but older adults with sensitive or thin skin should monitor for increased irritation.
